concepts.maxim: Treat others as you would wish to be treated.
concepts.summary: Perhaps the most widely shared rule for living. Long before these traditions could read one another, each arrived at the same quiet test: before you act, put yourself in the other person's place.

concepts.maxim: Life contains suffering; begin by accepting it.
concepts.summary: Not a counsel of despair, but a starting point. Naming the hardness of life honestly frees us to respond to it with courage rather than surprise.

concepts.maxim: Craving is the root of suffering.
concepts.summary: Much of our pain comes not from what happens, but from our grasping for things to be otherwise. Loosen the grip and the weight lightens.

concepts.maxim: Be present: the here and now is where life happens.
concepts.summary: The past has gone and the future has not arrived. The present moment is the only place we can actually live, act and enjoy.

concepts.maxim: Treat yourself like someone you are responsible for helping.
concepts.summary: We often care better for others than for ourselves. Extend the same kindness and discipline inward.

concepts.maxim: Find meaning in the struggle itself.
concepts.summary: Sisyphus pushes his boulder up the hill forever. The ancient myth was a punishment; the modern reading asks whether the effort itself can be enough.

concepts.maxim: Leave things better than you found them.
concepts.summary: A simple measure for a day, a campsite or a life: did the world come out a little ahead for your having passed through?

concepts.maxim: Keep it simple.
concepts.summary: Complexity is costly and fragile. The simplest design that works is usually the one that lasts.

concepts.maxim: A few causes drive most results (the 80/20 rule).
concepts.summary: Effort and outcome are rarely in proportion. Find the vital few things that matter and give them your best attention.

concepts.maxim: People rise to their level of incompetence.
concepts.summary: A gently humbling observation about organisations: we tend to be promoted until we land in a role we no longer do well. Know your strengths.

concepts.maxim: Happiness is reality minus expectations.
concepts.summary: A popular modern formula. When expectations outrun reality, disappointment fills the gap; holding them lightly leaves room for contentment.

concepts.maxim: Do your work wholeheartedly and with skill.
concepts.summary: Whatever is in front of you, give it your full strength. Skill grows quietly out of repeated, careful effort, and in time it opens doors.

concepts.maxim: Pursue what is meaningful, not what is merely profitable.
concepts.summary: Chase the thing that matters to you rather than the quick reward. A life built around meaning tends to carry its own momentum.

concepts.maxim: Ability grows with effort; measure yourself against who you were yesterday.
concepts.summary: Talents are a starting point, not a verdict. The useful comparison is with your own past self, and every honest effort moves the line.

concepts.maxim: More choice does not always mean more happiness.
concepts.summary: An endless menu can leave us anxious and second-guessing. Sometimes choosing 'good enough' and letting go is the wiser path.

concepts.maxim: There is a time for everything; give your days a rhythm.
concepts.summary: Life moves in seasons and cycles. A steady rhythm of rising, working, eating and resting makes room for everything else.

concepts.maxim: Tell the truth, or at least don't lie.
concepts.summary: Honesty keeps our footing sure. Each small truth makes the world, and ourselves, a little easier to trust.

concepts.maxim: Your thoughts shape your life.
concepts.summary: What we dwell on becomes the lens we see through, and then the ground we stand on. Tending the mind is tending the life.

concepts.maxim: Seek the middle way; avoid extremes.
concepts.summary: Too much and too little both lead us astray. Again and again the old teachers point to a balanced path between the extremes, harder to find than either, but steadier to walk.

concepts.maxim: Meet hatred with love and evil with good.
concepts.summary: Answering harm with harm only keeps the wheel turning. Many traditions ask something harder and braver: to break the cycle by returning kindness, even to an enemy.

concepts.maxim: Know yourself.
concepts.summary: Understanding the world begins close to home. To look honestly at our own motives, limits and ignorance is a lifelong task, and perhaps the beginning of every other kind of wisdom.

concepts.maxim: Be humble; pride goes before a fall.
concepts.summary: Those who lift themselves up tend to be brought low, while those who hold themselves lightly are trusted and remembered. Humility is not thinking less of ourselves, but seeing ourselves truly.

concepts.maxim: Be slow to anger; master yourself.
concepts.summary: Anger arrives quickly and leaves damage behind it. Real strength, these voices agree, lies less in overpowering others than in holding the reins of our own temper.

concepts.maxim: Remember that you will die, and live well today.
concepts.summary: Our days are numbered, and remembering it is not morbid but clarifying. Keeping death in view shrinks petty quarrels and turns us back towards what is good while we still can.

concepts.maxim: Speak kindly, or keep silent.
concepts.summary: Words can heal or wound, and once spoken they cannot be taken back. A little restraint in speech spares others pain and spares us a good deal of trouble.
